MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the next number in the pattern 11, 14, 17, 20, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 23
   B. 26
   C. 24
   D. 22

2. Round 47 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 50
   B. 60
   C. 0
   D. 40

3. What is the total value of the digit 5 in 7,250? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 500
   C. 10
   D. 50

4. In the number 6,092, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tens
   C. Thousands
   D. Hundreds

5. How many factors does 36 have? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 11
   C. 10
   D. 8

6. Work out 3,568 + 2,276. (1 mark)
   A. 5,844
   B. 5,854
   C. 5,734
   D. 5,744

7. Work out 5,127 + 2,864. (1 mark)
   A. 7,891
   B. 8,001
   C. 7,981
   D. 7,991

8. When we subtract 1,236 from 4,000, what do we do first? (1 mark)
   A. Add 1,236 to 4,000
   B. Subtract the thousands digits only
   C. Take the smaller digit from the bigger digit in each column
   D. Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds

9. Njeri had Ksh 5,000 and bought a bag for Ksh 1,850. How much money does she have left? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 3,140
   B. Ksh 4,850
   C. Ksh 3,150
   D. Ksh 3,250

10. Work out 9,250 − 4,875. (1 mark)
   A. 4,375
   B. 4,275
   C. 4,385
   D. 5,625

11. What is 34 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 134
   B. 340
   C. 34,000
   D. 3,400

12. To check 32 × 3 = 96 using division we work out (1 mark)
   A. 32 ÷ 3
   B. 96 ÷ 3
   C. 96 ÷ 32 × 3
   D. 96 − 32

13. What is 48 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 13
   B. 12
   C. 22
   D. 11

14. Change 2 1/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 6/3
   B. 3/3
   C. 7/3
   D. 8/3

15. Beth writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 1/2
   B. 2/9
   C. 11/5
   D. 3 1/2

16. In the fraction 3/4, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 4
   C. 7
   D. 3

17. A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts and 1 of the parts is shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 1/6
   B. 6/1
   C. 5/6
   D. 1/5

18. A circle is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 3/2
   B. 5/3
   C. 2/5
   D. 3/5

19. Which expression shows "n subtracted from 20"? (1 mark)
   A. 20 + n
   B. n − 20
   C. 20n
   D. 20 − n

20. Simplify 7x − 4x. (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 28x
   C. 3x
   D. 11x

21. If m = 7, what is the value of 6m? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 13
   C. 42
   D. 67

22. The relationship between metres and centimetres is (1 mark)
   A. 1 m = 1,000 cm
   B. 1 m = 100 cm
   C. 1 cm = 100 m
   D. 1 m = 10 cm

23. A pencil starts at the 3 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 11 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 9 cm
   B. 14 cm
   C. 8 cm
   D. 11 cm

24. A farmer plants seedlings 50 cm apart. How long is a row with 9 gaps between the seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. 5 m 50 cm
   B. 4 m 5 cm
   C. 450 m
   D. 4 m 50 cm

25. Musa covers a book cover with 12 rows of 9 squares. Which sum gives the number of squares? (1 mark)
   A. 12 − 9
   B. 12 ÷ 9
   C. 12 + 9
   D. 12 × 9

26. Rectangle P has 4 rows and 9 columns. Rectangle Q has 5 rows and 8 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle P
   B. They are equal
   C. It cannot be told
   D. Rectangle Q

27. A floor is covered with square tiles in 8 rows of 12 tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. 104 tiles
   B. 20 tiles
   C. 86 tiles
   D. 96 tiles

28. How many small cubes make a big cube that is 2 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks high? (1 mark)
   A. 16
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 4

29. A cuboid is 8 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 88 blocks
   B. 80 blocks
   C. 16 blocks
   D. 15 blocks

30. The unit for volume when each block has sides of 1 cm is (1 mark)
   A. square centimetres
   B. litres
   C. cubic centimetres
   D. centimetres

31. A cuboid has a volume of 72 blocks. One layer has 24 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 48
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 96

32. What is 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 L
   B. 2 3/4 L
   C. 2 L
   D. 2 1/4 L

33. What is 1/2 L + 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 1 1/4 L
   B. 3/4 L
   C. 1/2 L
   D. 1 L

34. What is 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 3/4 kg
   B. 6 1/4 kg
   C. 7 kg
   D. 6 1/2 kg

35. Two 1/4 kg masses balance (1 mark)
   A. 1 kg
   B. 3/4 kg
   C. 1/4 kg
   D. 1/2 kg

36. What is 2 h 45 min + 1 h 30 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 15 min
   B. 4 h 25 min
   C. 4 h 15 min
   D. 4 h 5 min

37. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 8 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 10. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 8:50
   B. 10:40
   C. 9:50
   D. 8:10

38. How many cents are in Ksh 3? (1 mark)
   A. 103 cents
   B. 300 cents
   C. 30 cents
   D. 3,000 cents

39. A bottle top is usually tightened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. sideways
   B. up and down
   C. clockwise
   D. anticlockwise

40. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many are NOT lorry? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 10
   C. 9
   D. 1

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Njoki has 9 halves of oranges. How many whole oranges is that? Write your answer as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

42. Draw a rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide and label its sides. (3 marks)

43. Amina has a 3 L jug of water. She pours 1 1/4 L into a pot and 1/2 L into a cup. How much water is left in the jug? (4 marks)

44. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

45. List three properties of a square. (3 marks)

46. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks and cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Work out both volumes and say which is greater. (4 marks)

47. Divide 450 by 100 and give the remainder. Explain what the remainder means. (4 marks)

48. Explain how to prepare a shopping list of three items and find its total cost. (4 marks)

49. A matatu carries m passengers. At a stop 8 get in and 3 get out. Write and simplify an expression for the number of passengers now. (3 marks)

50. Find the first common multiple of 4 and 6 by writing the first six multiples of each number. (4 marks)

51. A hall floor is covered with 12 rows of 15 square tiles. (a) How many tiles cover the floor? (b) A smaller room has 9 rows of 12 tiles. How many more tiles does the hall need than the smaller room? (5 marks)

52. A garden bed has 9 rows and 4 columns of 1 m squares. Find its area in square metres. (2 marks)

53. Using each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once, write the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers you can make. (4 marks)

54. A tank holds 20 L of water. In the morning 4 1/2 L is taken out and in the afternoon 3 3/4 L is taken out. How much water is left in the tank? (5 marks)

55. A buyer picks biscuits at Ksh 50, juice at Ksh 80 and a book at Ksh 120. He pays with a Ksh 500 note. Find the total cost and his change. (4 marks)

56. Draw a rectangle of 3 rows and 5 columns of squares. Write its area. (3 marks)

57. Write 0.8 and 0.37 as fractions. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 23
   The rule is add 3. 20 + 3 = 23.

2. A — 50
   Look at the ones digit 7. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 47 rounds to 50.

3. D — 50
   The digit 5 is in the tens place, so its total value is 5 × 10 = 50.

4. C — Thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 6 is in the thousands place.

5. A — 9
   The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. There are 9 of them.

6. A — 5,844
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,568 + 2,276 = 5,844.

7. D — 7,991
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 5,127 + 2,864 = 7,991.

8. D — Regroup from the thousands because there are zeros in the tens and hundreds
   The ones digit 0 is smaller than 6 and the tens and hundreds are zeros, so we borrow from the thousands.

9. C — Ksh 3,150
   Subtract 5,000 − 1,850 = 3,150. Check by adding: 3,150 + 1,850 = 5,000.

10. A — 4,375
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 9,250 − 4,875 = 4,375. Check: 4,375 + 4,875 = 9,250.

11. D — 3,400
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 34 × 100 = 3,400.

12. B — 96 ÷ 3
   Division undoes multiplication: 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

13. B — 12
   4 × 12 = 48, so 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

14. C — 7/3
   2 × 3 = 6 and 6 + 1 = 7. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 7/3.

15. C — 11/5
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 11/5 is one whole or more.

16. B — 4
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

17. A — 1/6
   The whole has 6 equal parts and 1 are shaded, so 1/6 is shaded.

18. D — 3/5
   Not shaded: 5 − 2 = 3 parts, so 3/5.

19. D — 20 − n
   The key words tell us the operation. "n subtracted from 20" is written 20 − n.

20. C — 3x
   Only like terms can be joined. 7x − 4x = 3x.

21. C — 42
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 42.

22. B — 1 m = 100 cm
   There are 100 centimetres in one metre.

23. C — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

24. D — 4 m 50 cm
   9 × 50 = 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm.

25. D — 12 × 9
   Squares = rows × columns = 12 × 9 = 108.

26. D — Rectangle Q
   P = 4 × 9 = 36 and Q = 5 × 8 = 40. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

27. D — 96 tiles
   8 × 12 = 96 tiles.

28. B — 8
   2 × 2 = 4 in a layer and 4 × 2 = 8 blocks.

29. B — 80 blocks
   One layer has 8 × 2 = 16 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 16 × 5 = 80 blocks.

30. C — cubic centimetres
   Each block is one cubic centimetre, so volume is measured in cubic centimetres.

31. B — 3
   Layers = 72 ÷ 24 = 3.

32. D — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 5 1/2 L − 3 1/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

33. B — 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 1/2 L + 1/4 L = 3/4 L.

34. D — 6 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg = 6 1/2 kg.

35. D — 1/2 kg
   1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

36. C — 4 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 4 h 15 min.

37. A — 8:50
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 10 shows 10 × 5 = 50 minutes, so the time is 8:50.

38. B — 300 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 3 = 3 × 100 = 300 cents.

39. C — clockwise
   Tightening a bottle top means turning it clockwise.

40. C — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/2 oranges
   Working / marking points: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1 (2 marks); 4 1/2 (1 mark).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle with two sides 6 cm and two sides 3 cm and square corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four straight sides with square corners, 1 mark for correct lengths, 1 mark for labels.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: 1 1/4 + 1/2 = 1 3/4 L used (2 marks); 3 − 1 3/4 = 1 1/4 L (2 marks).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 kg (1 mark); total 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Four equal sides, four right angles and four lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct property.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A = 40 blocks, B = 60 blocks. B is greater by 20 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the volumes, 1 mark for the comparison, 1 mark for the difference.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 remainder 50. There are 4 whole hundreds in 450 and 50 is left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4, 1 mark for remainder 50, 2 marks for the explanation.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what is needed, write the three items with numbers, find the price of each, work out the cost of each item, and add the costs to get the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for choosing items, 1 mark for writing quantity, 1 mark for prices, 1 mark for adding the costs.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: m + 8 − 3 = m + 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for m + 8, 1 mark for taking away 3, 1 mark for simplifying to m + 5.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The first common multiple is 12.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct list and 2 marks for identifying 12.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 180 tiles (b) 72 more tiles
   Working / marking points: (a) 12 × 15: 12 × 10 = 120 and 12 × 5 = 60, so 180 (2 marks); smaller room 9 × 12 = 108 (1 mark); 180 − 108 (1 mark); 72 tiles (1 mark).

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: 36 square metres
   Working / marking points: 9 × 4 = 36. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for the unit.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Largest: 7,420. Smallest: 2,047.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 7,420 (digits in descending order). 2 marks for 2,047 (a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0).

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: 11 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Total taken: 4 1/2 + 3 3/4 = 4 2/4 + 3 3/4 = 7 5/4 = 8 1/4 L (3 marks). 20 − 8 1/4 = 11 3/4 L (2 marks).

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Total Ksh 250; change Ksh 250
   Working / marking points: 50 + 80 + 120 = 250 (2 marks); 500 − 250 = 250 (2 marks).

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with 3 rows of 5 squares; area = 15 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 rows, 1 mark for 5 columns, 1 mark for area 15.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8/10 and 37/100
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fraction.
